name: Max Factor ice mask

card.summary: A plastic mask studded with water-fillable cubes that was frozen and worn on the face as a cooling, rejuvenating treatment.
card.note: A vintage 1940s-era novelty; frozen items should not be pressed directly on skin for long.

quick.overview:
The Max Factor ice mask is a 1940s-era facial device: a plastic mask studded with small compartments shaped like ice cubes. Users filled them with water, froze the mask, and applied it to the face as a rejuvenating treatment.

The cold is the appearance mechanism, as with other cooling treatments used to calm puffiness and refresh the look of skin. A beauty-history blog describes it as popular with Hollywood stars and nicknamed "Hangover Heaven".
quick.how: Fill the cube compartments with water, freeze, then wear it on the face for a short period, as described in historical accounts.
quick.risks: Prolonged contact between frozen items and skin can cause cold injury; accounts of the mask describe it as a novelty rather than a clinically tested product.

lead: The Max Factor ice mask is a vintage beauty device: a plastic face mask studded with plastic "ice cubes" that users filled with water and froze before wearing it as a rejuvenating facial treatment.[1] A beauty-history blog places it among 1940s Hollywood treatments and says it was nicknamed "Hangover Heaven".[1]
The idea is that sustained cold refreshes the face, the same logic behind ice rolling and cold compresses today. No studies of this specific mask were found.
